A real shell command, exactly as if typed at a terminal

questions.q: What does `{{ ds }}` resolve to inside a bash_command string?
options: A random unique identifier
The current server timestamp down to the millisecond
The name of the DAG itself
The DAG run's logical date, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD
questions.explain: ds is a built-in Airflow template variable resolving to the DAG run's logical date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

questions.q: What determines whether a BashOperator task succeeds or fails?
options: The shell command's exit code — 0 succeeds, anything else fails
The task always succeeds regardless of the command's outcome
A separate success/failure flag you must set manually
Whether the command printed any output at all
questions.explain: Task success or failure maps directly to the shell command's exit code, exactly as it would at a real terminal.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should you reach for BashOperator instead of PythonOperator?
options: When calling an existing CLI tool or script that already does the job
Never — PythonOperator should always be preferred
Always, regardless of what the task does
Only when the task involves no external tools at all
